title: The Thief Who Stole My Heart
hookLine: a father finds milk on his small son's lips and demands to know who fed him
carry: grace comes first: shiva steals the heart
last: WE BELONG TO SHIVA, NOT TO FEAR.

cards: Who gave you this milk? A father stands over his small son on the steps of a temple tank, and he's angry. He went down into the water to bathe and left the boy on the bank.
Now he's come up, there's milk on the child's lips, and nobody else in sight. He raises a stick. Who fed you?
The boy doesn't cry or make an excuse. He lifts his hand, points up at the sky, and starts to sing. Today, another of the Tevaram's three singers: Sambandar.

teach.h: A CHILD ALONE ON THE BANK
teach.b: The Periya Puranam tells it, in paraphrase. The town is Sirkazhi, in the Tamil country. While his father is under the water, the child, alone, cries out for his mother and father.
Shiva and the Goddess appear above the tank.
She fills a golden cup with her own milk, mixed with divine wisdom, and gives it to him. Then they're gone, and the father comes up the steps.

teach.h: THE THIEF WHO STOLE MY HEART
teach.b: The boy's song begins, in paraphrase: the one with an earring in his ear, who rides the bull, who wears the pure white crescent moon, smeared with the ash of the burning ground, he is the thief who stole my heart.
He lives here, in this town. Asked who fed him, the boy gives a portrait, the way you'd describe someone you'd just seen up close. Then that phrase: the thief who stole my heart.
A strange thing to call God, and a tender one. The boy didn't earn the milk. He cried, and it came.
Shiva takes the heart first, and the song comes after. Tamil Shaivas have a word for this: arul, grace. God moves first; worship is the answer, not the price.
And notice where the song ends: in this town, here. The Tevaram's hymns name their temples, and Tamil Shaivas still go on pilgrimage to the places they sing.
His father came up the steps to scold him, and went home with a hymn.

how: Sambandar's hymns are sung by oduvars, the singers of Tamil Shaiva temples, and the story of the milk at the temple tank is told at Sirkazhi, the town of his birth.

games.q: what does “tamil shaivism and the tevaram” mean?
o: the milk offered to Shiva in every Tamil temple
a Tamil lullaby sung over children at the temple tank
Tamil hymns to Shiva, each naming the place where he lives

games.q: the boy at the temple tank — tap the pairs.
p: came up from the water angry
gave milk in a golden cup

s: the boy earned the Goddess's milk by being good
he only cried out, and it came. in Tamil Shaivism grace, arul, moves first, and the song answers it.
the song calls Shiva the thief who stole his heart
Shiva takes the heart first, and the song comes after.
the hymn ends far from any particular place
it ends here, in his own town, like the Tevaram's other place-hymns.

games.q: you're the small boy. your father comes up from the water, sees milk on your lips, and raises a stick: who fed you?
o: point to the sky and sing.
games.why: Sambandar points up and sings his first hymn, a portrait of Shiva, the thief who stole his heart.

practice: Ask yourself quietly what has stolen your heart lately, not what ought to have, but what actually did: a face, a piece of music, a view from a window. Notice that you didn't earn it. It came first, and you answered.
If you pray, give one line back to God today, a thank-you or a verse, the way the boy sang back to Shiva. If you don't, say the thank-you to whoever brought it to you.

wordCard.voice: Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram: Sambandar, fed by the Goddess, who answered his angry father with a song. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: grace comes first. Shiva steals the heart, and the song comes after. Go gently.
